tools.name: search_local_workers
tools.description: Find a real person near someone in the US who does a kind of home job or errand: assembly, yard work, cleaning, moving help, hauling, small repairs, pickups. Searches locals on GigNGo by service and place. Returns public profiles: name, bio, skills, prices the local set, reviews, whether they filmed

tools.name: get_worker_profile
tools.description: Get the public profile of one GigNGo local by their profile slug. Returns name, bio, skills, prices the local set, reviews, whether they filmed their work, neighbor vouches, self-reported badges, service area, availability, a profile URL and `limits` (GigNGo runs no background checks). Slugs come fr

tools.name: get_work_record
tools.description: Get a local's Work Record: evidence of their work, where every item says how GigNGo knows it. Evidence types: filmed (clips our check says show the work, not who is in them), homeowner_confirmed / local_reported / inferred_from_messages (finished jobs, counted), neighbor_vouched, recorded_on_gigngo

tools.name: find_work_clips
tools.description: Find short videos of locals doing a kind of job, e.g. "deck building", "pressure washing", "house cleaning". Every clip was checked to show someone actually doing the work. Returns a watch page URL (link people there), an embed URL, the local's first name and town, the job's search words, and the lo

tools.name: draft_job_post
tools.description: Use this when someone needs a local to do a job or errand for them (put furniture together, mow a lawn, help move, pick something up, wait in line) and wants it posted. Draft the job post and get back a link THEY open to review and post it. Posting is free. You cannot hire, book or pay anyone throug

tools.name: list_service_categories
tools.description: List all 30 GigNGo service categories with their slugs (e.g. "house-cleaning", "electrician", "moving-help"). Call this to discover valid values for the `service` parameter of search_local_workers and the `category` parameter of browse_open_tasks.

tools.name: check_service_availability
tools.description: Check which of the 30 service categories have public locals in a US state or city, with a count per service. Useful before searching, or to answer "can I get X done in Y?". State is required (full name, lowercase, hyphens: "new-jersey"); city is optional — omit it for state-level availability.

tools.name: browse_open_tasks
tools.description: Browse open jobs homeowners have posted on GigNGo that locals can apply to. Each task includes title, description, `details` (the poster's Additional Details note, present on most jobs and usually the most specific part), category, budget, approximate location (coordinates are privacy-offset), when

tools.name: get_area_demand_density
tools.description: Find which US cities are actually converting: how many jobs each area posted, how many locals applied, what share of jobs got any reply at all, and the median hours to the first applicant. Ranked by a "heat" score that combines applicant density with response reliability, shrunk toward the platform

tools.name: get_platform_info
tools.description: Get an overview of GigNGo: what it is, what it does not do (limits), service category count, how jobs reach locals, iOS/Android app links, and API documentation URLs. Call this for general "what is GigNGo" questions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_local_workers, get_worker_profile, get_work_record, find_work_clips, draft_job_post, get_platform_info · Private data: get_work_record · Public sink: draft_job_post, get_area_demand_density · Destructive: draft_job_post.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_local_workers, get_worker_profile, get_work_record, find_work_clips, draft_job_post, get_platform_info · Private data: get_work_record · Public sink: draft_job_post, get_area_demand_density · Destructive: draft_job_post

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
